messages.author: fbff4100433066b4
messages.subject: counting/plotting divergent transitions
parts: If I have many stan_fit models (saved as rds files), is there any programmatic way to find out which model has divergent transitions? I have not been able to find an stan_method to count/plot divergent transitions? Certainly there is one way which is shinystan but then I will to manually open all models one at a time. It would be nice if the stan_diag plot showed the divergent transitions just like shinystan does.

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] counting/plotting divergent transitions
parts:
If you also want plots then I recommend checking out our new bayesplot package, which has several available plotting functions that give you some information about divergences. 

The mcmc_nuts_divergence function compares the shape of lp__  (log-posterior up to constant) when there's a divergence (if there are any) to the distribution when there is no divergence. If there are divergences then you'll likely see that lp|divergence=1 will have much lighter tails than lp|divergence=0. 

The mcmc_trace function now also accepts an optional argument divergences. If specified it will add a rug plot below the trace plot indicating the approximate location of the divergences. 

Finally, the mcmc_pairs function (not yet released but available to try out) will indicate divergences as red points. 

Jonah
